references.text: Moses appeals to God's name and glory when he prays for the people of Israel, just as Joshua does here. Both pray that God will act for the sake of His great name.
Moses argues that the surrounding nations will hear about Israel's defeat and draw conclusions about God's power, a concern also expressed by Joshua here.
Moses warns that other peoples will say the Lord was unable to bring Israel into the land, paralleling Joshua's fear of what the nations will say.
Describes the Canaanites and other peoples in the land who would hear about and react to Israel's actions, something Joshua fears in his prayer.
Samuel says that the Lord will not abandon His people for the sake of His great name, the same theme concerning God's name and glory.
God acts for the sake of His name and holds back His wrath, a concept also appealed to by Joshua.
God acts for the sake of His name so that it is not profaned among the nations, paralleling Joshua's concern for God's great name.
